newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close up on thin local funds support.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close up on thin local funds support.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chips closed slightly firmer on Tuesday following selective blue-chip buying by local institutions, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 4.86 points, 0.55 percent, higher at 885.31, after peaking at 894.03. The small-capitalised Second Board index shed 2.74 points, 0.59 percent, to 464.01.
"There has been some selective blue-chip nibbling by local funds," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
Air courier Transmile fell 4.60 ringgit to 17.70 ringgit, after being suspended since July 28.
Dealers said Transmile's fall reflected the overall market's near 14-percent slide since the stock was suspended.
On Monday, shipping company Konsortium announced plans to acquire a 35 percent stake in Transmile's subsidiary Transmile Air. Konsortium closed unchanged at 10.30.

Lingering concerns over the direction of the ringgit's value against the dollar kept investors from entering the market, even though valutations are at their lowest levels in nerly two years, said dealers.
Market volume stood at 221 million shares, valued at 1,363 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 417 to 217.
Among the most actively traded stocks were Telekom, Sime Darby and Magnum, rising between eight and 15 cents.
The issues have a total weightage of around 17 percent.
The ringgit continued to be weak on Tuesday, trading at 2.7860 against the U.S. dollar at 0952 GMT, but came off its earlier low of 2.8005.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract gained 17 points to 871.0 with 1,456 lots traded. September futures rose 16 points to 872.0 with 57 lots having changed hands.
